carryForwards.CF-D1: Reservation is taken inside B's synchronous guard and released on the guard's refusal return or in onCommitted, both in the same synchronous span; D makes no M write; no await between reserve and those releases
carryForwards.CF-D2: Explicit release on the guard refusal return and in onCommitted; the microtask is only the safety net (and afterRelease releases idempotently). Residual, disclosed: when the guard admits but the append itself then reports a revision conflict or throws, B's adapter does not call onCommitted, so M is released by C's microtask; no D-owned seam can release earlier without editing B leaves
carryForwards.CF-D3: reserveMatchProgression() is called in try/catch inside the guard; any throw (including the idle-connection refusal) returns {kind:refused, reason:progression-reservation-busy}, never commit-uncertain
carryForwards.CF-D4: C IMMEDIATE (writer .immediate()) then M (reservation in the guard); never M before C; neither held across an await
carryForwards.CF-D5: No deferred read-then-write on M; the guard only reads (strict saga precedence) on the reserved M connection
carryForwards.CF-D6: No presence-only readback added; committed/uncertain classification stays B's
carryForwards.CF-D7: onCommitted is always requested (forces the writer in-transaction refusal); M in a transaction before BEGIN is a typed refusal
